overview: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) is a Central Sector Scheme launched by the Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, to mobilize a medium- to long-term debt financing facility for investment in viable post-harvest management infrastructure and farming assets. It provides financial support through interest subvention and credit guarantee to eligible beneficiaries including farmers, FPOs, agri-entrepreneurs, startups, and others. The scheme aims to improve agriculture infrastructure, reduce post-harvest losses, enhance farmer income, and strengthen the agricultural value chain across India.
target_beneficiaries: national and state federations of cooperatives
central/state agency or local body sponsored PPP projects
objectives: Improved marketing infrastructure to allow farmers to sell directly to a larger base of consumers and increase value realization
With investments in logistics infrastructure, farmers will be able to sell in the market with reduced post-harvest losses and a smaller number of intermediaries
With modern packaging and cold storage system access, farmers will be able to further decide when to sell in the market and improve realization
Viable farming assets for improved productivity and optimization of inputs will result in substantial savings to farmers
Government will be able to direct priority sector lending in currently unviable projects by supporting through interest subvention, incentive through convergence and credit guarantee

Due to improvements in post-harvest infrastructure, government will further be able to reduce national food wastage percentage thereby enable agriculture sector to become competitive with current global levels
Central/State Government Agencies or local bodies will be able to structure viable projects on their own or PPP projects for attracting investment in agriculture infrastructure
With a dedicated source of funding, entrepreneurs will push for innovation in agriculture sector by leveraging new age technologies including IoT, AI, etc.
It will also connect the players in ecosystem and hence, improve avenues for collaboration between entrepreneurs and farmers

With Credit Guarantee, convergence and interest subvention lending institutions will be able to lend with a lower risk. This scheme will help to enlarge their customer base and diversification of portfolio
Refinance facility will enable larger role for cooperative banks and RRBs
With reduced inefficiencies in post-harvest ecosystem, key benefit for consumers will be a larger share of produce reaching the market and hence, better quality and prices
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries include Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Marketing Cooperative Societies, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self Help Groups (SHGs), Farmers, Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), Multipurpose Cooperative Societies, Agri-entrepreneurs, Startups, Central/State agency or Local Body sponsored Public Private Partnership Projects, State Agencies, Agricultural Produce Market Committees (Mandis), National & State Federations of Cooperatives, Federations of FPOs, and Federations of Self Help Groups (SHGs).
benefits: Financial benefits include interest subvention of 3% per annum up to a limit of ₹2 crore for a maximum period of 7 years, and credit guarantee coverage for loans up to ₹2 crore under the CGTMSE scheme with the government paying the fee. Non-financial benefits include convergence with various Central and State Government schemes (MIDH, PMFME, SMAM, GOBAR-Dhan, PMKSY, AMI, PACS as MSC, RKVY, PMEGP, PM-KUSUM), online single window facility in collaboration with participating lending institutions, and Project Management Unit (PMU) support for handholding in project preparation.
financial_support: The financing facility provides loans up to ₹2 crore per project per location, with interest subvention of 3% per annum capped at ₹2 crore per project, available for a maximum period of 7 years. Credit guarantee coverage is available for loans up to ₹2 crore under the CGTMSE scheme, with the government bearing the fee. For loans exceeding ₹2 crore, interest subvention is limited to ₹2 crore. The scheme has a total size of ₹1 lakh crore, and repayment period covers a maximum of 7 years including a moratorium period of up to 2 years.
application_process: 1. Visit the AIF portal at https://agriinfra.dac.gov.in 2. Register as a beneficiary through the Beneficiary Registration section 3. Prepare a Detailed Project Report (DPR) using the template provided 4. Approach a participating lending institution (Commercial Banks, Cooperative Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, NCDC, NBFCs etc.) with the DPR 5. The lending institution processes the loan application under the AIF scheme 6. Upon sanction, the loan is disbursed by the lending institution 7. Interest subvention and credit guarantee claims are submitted through the AIF portal
required_documents: Bank’s loan application form / Customer Request Letter for AIF Loan duly filled and signed
Passport size photographs of the promoter/partners/director
Identity proof – Voter ID card/PAN card/Aadhaar card/Driving license
Address Proof : Residence: Voter ID card/Passport/Aadhaar card/Driving license/Electricity Bill/Latest property Tax Bill
Business Office/Registered Office: Electricity Bill/Latest Property Tax Receipt/Certificate of Incorporation in case of Companies/Certificate of Registration in case of partnership Firms

Proof of Registration: In case of Company : Article of Association; In case of Partnership : Certificate of Registration of Firm with Registrar of Firm; In case of MSMEs : Certificate of Registration with District Industries Centre (DIC)/Udyog Aadhar
Income Tax Return for last three years, If available
Audited Balance Sheet of last 3 Years, If available
ROC Search Report of the Company
Copy of Bank Statement for last one year (If available)
Repayment track record of existing loans (Loan Statement)
Local authority permissions, Layout plans/estimates, Building sanction
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted year-round.
implementing_agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
caveats: Interest subvention of 3% p.a. is limited to ₹2 crore per project in one location, though loan amount can be higher
For a private sector entity, such as farmer, agri entrepreneur, start-up there will be a limit of maximum of 25 such projects
Limitation of 25 projects will not be applicable to state agencies, national and state federations of cooperatives, federations of FPOs and federation of SHGs
Standalone secondary processing infrastructures are not eligible
Not eligible for individuals/farmers for certain infrastructure components (Note 4)

Component-A of PM-KUSUM eligible for Individual farmers/ Group of farmers/ FPOs/ Cooperatives/ Panchayats to set up solar power plants of capacity up to 2 MW on barren/cultivable/uncultivable/pasturelands or marshy lands
